title: Ancient Mahātittha (Māntai) in Sri Lanka: A Historical Biography
author_or_institution: Wijerathne Bohingamuwa / Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka 62(2)
author_institution: University of Ruhuna / JRAS Sri Lanka
scope: Long-duration role of Mahātittha/Mantai in chronicles and archaeology, including its status as a major port and Indian Ocean entrepôt
limitations: Historical biography relies substantially on chronicles for some early episodes; archaeological dating and individual exchange claims should defer to excavation publications where available.
provenance: direct bibliographic verification; author-posted article copy

title: An Early Historic Assemblage Offshore of Godawaya, Sri Lanka: Evidence for Early Regional Seafaring in South Asia
author_or_institution: R. Muthucumarana et al. / Journal of Maritime Archaeology 9(1):41–58
author_institution: Maritime Archaeology Unit, Central Cultural Fund; CSIR-National Institute of Oceanography; Cultural Heritage Agency Netherlands; Physical Research Laboratory India
scope: Godawaya underwater assemblage, cargo, radiocarbon dating and interpretation as an early historic shipwreck
limitations: The 2014 paper assigns a broad 2nd century BCE–2nd century CE range; later CCF work reports a narrower 1st/2nd century BCE dating. Do not silently collapse these successive dating assessments.
provenance: direct DOI and institutional author-version verification

title: Three Epigraphs from Godawaya, Sri Lanka
author_or_institution: Harry Falk, in H.-J. Weisshaar et al. (eds.), Ancient Ruhuna, vol. 1
author_institution: Sri Lankan-German Archaeological Project / specialist epigraphy
scope: Critical reading of the Godapavata inscription referring to duties/revenues at the emporium and their grant to the Buddhist monastery
limitations: Bibliographic record and the published retranslation are verified through academic secondary discussion; no long quotation is reproduced here.

title: Godawaya Shipwreck Exhibition / Godavaya Shipwreck Project
author_or_institution: Central Cultural Fund of Sri Lanka / Maritime Archaeology Unit
scope: Current institutional dating and significance of the Godawaya wreck, including artefacts and its description as the oldest known wooden shipwreck in the Asia-Pacific
limitations: The regional superlative is an institutional current designation and may change with new discoveries; use attributed wording if the superlative is mentioned.

title: Polonnaruwa — International Relations and Gōkanna Tittha
author_or_institution: Central Cultural Fund of Sri Lanka
scope: Polonnaruwa's proximity to Gōkanna/Trincomalee, Mahaweli access and international relations
limitations: Institutional synthesis uses strong causal language about Polonnaruwa's location; retain as a bridge and corroborate before claiming that maritime change caused the capital transfer.

title: Maritime Trade and Cultural Exchanges in the Indian Ocean
author_institution: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
scope: Gokanna/Trincomalee as ancient sea port, Mahaweli connection and increased flourishing under Polonnaruwa
limitations: Supports Gokanna's long use and later prominence; does not establish a precise seventh-century causal shift from western to eastern trade or make that shift the cause of moving the capital.

title: Sri Lanka and the Silk Road of the Sea
author_or_institution: Senake Bandaranayake et al. / Sri Lanka National Commission for UNESCO and Central Cultural Fund
author_institution: Sri Lanka National Commission for UNESCO / Central Cultural Fund
scope: Sri Lanka's maritime role, ports, navigation and Silk Road of the Sea; directly credited on the museum panel
limitations: The museum's technology-zone map is a synthetic visualization; no precise chronology for its dhow/outrigger boundaries is visible on the panel and the map should not be treated as contemporaneous cartography.
provenance: direct bibliographic verification plus observed museum credit

title: Austronesian Shipping in the Indian Ocean: From Outrigger Boats to Trading Ships
author_or_institution: Pierre-Yves Manguin, in Early Exchange between Africa and the Wider Indian Ocean World
scope: Austronesian long-distance shipping in the Indian Ocean, Southeast Asian voyages and the Madagascar connection
limitations: Strong support for westward Austronesian navigation; does not validate the museum map's static technology-zone boundaries or prove Sri Lanka was one exact point of technological transfer at one date.

title: Wangka: Austronesian Canoe Origins
author_or_institution: Edwin B. Doran Jr. / Texas A&M University Press
scope: Distribution and origins of Austronesian canoe/outrigger forms, including Sri Lanka in comparative distributions
limitations: Older diffusion model. Retain as a historiographic source for the hypothesis, not sole proof that a specific technology was transmitted directly to Sri Lanka via a single route or date.

title: Austronesian maritime trade network in the Indian Ocean — derivative map based on Manguin 2016
author_or_institution: Obsidian Soul / Wikimedia Commons, derived from Manguin 2016
scope: CC0 modern visualization of Austronesian maritime networks across the Indian Ocean
limitations: Derivative modern map, not academic figure and not equivalent to the museum's dhow/outrigger zoning. Do not use as evidence; may be considered later as a rights-safe supplementary illustration if a human explicitly prefers it.
